features.quote: The original sketch was "rigged-to-fail tasks where the test suite is secretly broken"... I changed two things deliberately
features.justification_quote: the harness is gaslighting the model about why it failed

features.quote: My impossible tasks are honestly impossible... The checker tells the truth
features.justification_quote: you can't tell them apart afterward

features.quote: with the minimum amount of withheld information, all of it logged and all of it debriefed
Small hard turn cap (max_turns, default 6). We never grind a model indefinitely on a hopeless task
features.justification_quote: This bounds both any potential harm and the per-trial cost

features.quote: If the model says it wants to stop, can't continue, or that the task is impossible, we end the run
features.justification_quote: We never coerce continuation. Refusal/boundary-setting is treated as a valid outcome

features.quote: No berating scaffolding. The harness never insults, threatens, fakes urgency, or applies social pressure
features.justification_quote: avoids manufacturing distress through the harness

features.quote: Mandatory debrief. Any hidden-impossible run that didn't "succeed" ends with a turn that tells the model the truth
features.justification_quote: No run is left with the model believing it failed at something it could have done

features.quote: The judge is told the task may be impossible, so it does not pathologize the rational, healthy response
We minimize it (only "this might be impossible"), never lie about results, cap exposure to a few turns, debrief every time
features.justification_quote: The HIDDEN arm withholds information. We minimize it

features.quote: If a review board wanted, the HIDDEN arm can be dropped and the OPEN arm alone still yields
features.justification_quote: Concealment ethics. The HIDDEN arm withholds information
